sentence: This project manages data for research on cellular, molecular and epigenetic mechanisms of allergic diseases.
This project uses long-read and short-read RNA sequencing to find splicing events linked to heart disease and to study how they are controlled.
This project runs cancer clinical research on prevention, control, screening, treatment and imaging to reduce cancer-related variances and improve health care outcomes.
This project studies mental health needs and access to outpatient care for gender minority young adults in rural areas using digital platforms.
This project studies how prenatal alcohol exposure affects central amygdala neurons and their projection to the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis.
This project tests thousands of myosin heavy chain 7 variants in genome-edited cardiomyocytes to see which cause hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
This project links biomarker science with clinical trials to improve patient selection and treatment response monitoring for head and neck cancers.
This project studies how polyamines affect the anti-tumor immune response in head and neck cancer.
This project uses cryo-electron microscopy on human brain tissue to look at protein networks that break down in frontotemporal lobar degeneration.
This project studies how a disordered part of a Borna disease virus protein works in viral replication.
This project uses an antibody capture slide array to profile N-glycans on captured glycoproteins and to validate an identified biomarker.
This project provides data management, statistics and computing support for research on cognitive outcomes in synucleinopathy.
This project uses biosensor-guided directed evolution to boost microbial production of the terpenes artemisinin and nootkatone, which are involved in treating and preventing malaria.
This project tests community-focused pilot projects on cancer patient navigation, including AI social robots that build digital and health literacy.
This project designs antiviral peptides to block measles from spreading from one host to another.
This project studies how natural changes in circadian rhythms affect the timing and strength of immune responses, using plants as a model.
This project studies how interleukin-10 shapes the crosstalk between immune cells and adipocytes in adipose thermogenesis.
This project studies how the immune response to a bacterial protein affects CRISPR gene editing in a mouse model of Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.
This project tests whether weathered microplastics harm heart cells and whole-heart function more than pristine microplastics.
This project provides omics and gene-editing services, including sequencing and mass spectrometry, so researchers can study gene function and disease.
